{{Short description|British mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=November 2017}}
{{Use British English|date=November 2017}}
'''Jacques Vanneste''' is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Edinburgh]], whose main research area is [[fluid dynamics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Jacques Vanneste {{!}} Edinburgh Fluid Dynamics Group |url=https://www.efdg.ed.ac.uk/people/jacques-vanneste |website=www.efdg.ed.ac.uk |access-date=10 July 2021}}</ref>

His particular research interest is in analytic methods for handling systems with dynamics on two distinct time or length scales.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~vanneste/research.shtml | title=Jacques Vanneste's research | accessdate=2010-05-12 }}</ref> This is relevant, for example, for the interaction between weather and ocean circulation, where fast [[inertial waves]] can be generated by slow underlying flows; see for example his work<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~vanneste/papers/tropopause.pdf | title = Quasi-geostrophic dynamics of a finite-depth tropopause | accessdate=2010-05-12}}</ref> on the [[tropopause]], and his most-cited paper.<ref>{{ cite journal | last1=Vanneste | first1=Jacques | last2=Yavneh | first2=Irad | year=2004 | title=Exponentially Small Inertia Gravity Waves and the Breakdown of Quasigeostrophic Balance | journal= Journal of the Atmospheric Sciences | volume=61 | issue=2 | pages=211&ndash;223 | doi=10.1175/1520-0469(2004)061<0211:ESIWAT>2.0.CO;2| doi-access=free }}</ref> He is also interested in the dynamics of [[:wikt:stir|stirring]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~vanneste/papers/wcdps3.pdf | title=What controls the decay of passive scalars in smooth flows? | accessdate=2010-05-12| date=2005-07-01}}</ref>

==Awards==
He is the recipient of the 2010 [[Adams Prize]].<ref name="2010w">{{cite web | url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/news/dp/2010022602 | title='Fluid Mechanics' work wins 2010 Adams Prize | date=2010-02-26 | accessdate=2010-02-26 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100305090629/http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/news/dp/2010022602 | archive-date=5 March 2010 | url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2014, Vanneste was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.rse.org.uk/fellow/jacques-vanneste/|title=Professor Jacques Vanneste FRSE - The Royal Society of Edinburgh|work=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|access-date=2018-02-09|language=en-GB}}</ref>
